podcast.title: Residency Offer to The Trews
podcast.body: Jeff Healey saw The Trews open for him in Halifax in the summer of 2001 and was impressed. He subsequently offered them a weekly residency as the house band at his new establishment, Jeff Healey's bar, on Bathurst and Queen in Toronto, performing every Thursday. "He really liked us. He said, look, I'm starting a bar called Healey's. You guys give me my house band every Thursday."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Trews: In Their Own Words

xref.title: Jeff Healey's Bar Residency (2001)
xref.body: Following an opening gig for Jeff Healey in Halifax in Summer 2001, Healey invited the band to be the house band at his new Toronto bar, Healey's, on Bathurst and Queen. The Trews accepted, playing every Thursday throughout Summer and Fall 2001. "He said, look, I'm starting a bar called Healey's. You guys give me my house band every Thursday."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Trews: In Their Own Words

xref.title: Larry Wanigas Management
xref.body: During their residency at Jeff Healey's bar, they caught the attention of legendary manager Larry Wanigas, known for managing k.d. lang and Big Sugar. Wanigas liked the band and introduced them to producer Gordy Johnson, leading to their first album. "Larry Wanigas who is the, you know, legendary manager, he managed Katie Lang and at the time he was managing big sugar."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
